scope: One group-level broader-profile context comparison using exactly six existing merged spectra, plus the two discovery exposures native orders2/3 and preserved raw context. It does not rerun completed mapping/epoch work or search new events.

frame_equations.native_barycentric: requested native topocentric wavelength = (cb + x) / (1 + BERV_epoch/c)
frame_equations.native_topocentric: requested native topocentric wavelength = ct + x

fixed_joint_geometry.reference_requirement: Both discovery-reference profiles must be sampled on this same joint grid and same BERV anchor. Do not preserve separate per-event center or anchor offsets from the old epoch tables.

scientific_reading_order: Start with original signed merged/native flux, wavelength coverage and data gaps before normalized panels. Order3 can be low or nonpositive despite no inherited merged low-continuum flag; geometry support and useful spectral signal are separate questions.

Use fixed flank medians as reference levels, not assumed line-free continua. Keep positive, nonpositive and missing medians explicit; only adequate positive reference levels may support normalized panels. Do not divide by absolute median, clip negatives or substitute a better-looking order.

Compare the fixed shared core and the broader surrounding pattern separately, against both discovery references. Zero-lag correlations and RMS can show whether the selected core follows the same spectral pattern as its surroundings; no lag/center/width search is justified.

Keep the surrounding pattern in the data. Root requested signed flux and fixed flank scaling rather than an additional fitted line-background that might remove relevant broad structure. No new Gaussian, free-width or continuum model is needed for this context task.

Maintain common finite-support masks per comparison and report support counts/coverage. Near native order3 edges, missing coverage remains missing; do not extrapolate or shrink the frozen window. Do not bridge gaps or the separation between flanks when computing adjacent-difference noise proxies.

Display both raw-order contexts with their original registration and gate history. Failed earlier local checks and later supported wider-reference checks both remain recorded; there is no new mapping fit or origin promotion.
interpretation_limits: The two event centers differ by0.0300Angstrom, about0.896 nominal resolution elements, and belong to one overlapping group. They are not two independent confirmations.

The six existing epochs span3.1932285753km/s, about1.224918 nominal resolution elements. Frame preference at this modest displacement is descriptive, not a calibrated discriminator or stellar-rest-frame identification.

Native e2ds and merged flux scales differ. Fixed-reference normalized amplitudes, frame-dependent normalization differences and native/merged ratios are not calibrated line fluxes. Positive scalar scaling alone does not alter Pearson correlation.
The historical fixed Gaussian width is a template parameter, not a measured linewidth. A calibrated free-width analysis would be a separate method and is outside this task.
Raw-order agreement cannot be claimed from an unusable order3 panel. Fixed broad correlations may be dominated by neighboring structure; core and surrounding-pattern results must both be shown.
Missing original positive ERR support and correlated samples prevent significance or physical-origin claims. All current U labels remain unchanged.
